chunks: If they turn away, We have not sent you as a warden over them. Upon you is only the delivery [of the message]. And when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if a misfortune strikes them for what their hands have put forward, then indeed man is ungrateful.

key_terms.الْبَلَاغُ: The delivery / conveying of the message

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's duty of delivery and being a warden over people?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the Prophet’s limited authority to compel faith, highlighting the distinction between conveying the divine message (balaagh) and guiding the heart, which remains with Allah. It reflects the human tendency toward ingratitude (kufr) when trials arise, a concept often linked to the Imams' role as guides who clarify the path without forcing acceptance. This reinforces the theological principle that while the Prophet is the perfect exemplar, his duty is proclamation, leaving the outcome to divine will.
